summary: Updates RFC 4181, Guidelines for Authors and Reviewers of MIB Documents, to recognize the creation of the IETF Trust. It is a Best Current Practice.

eli5.summary: A guide for writing management lists mentioned an old owner of the rights. This small update names the new owner, the IETF Trust.

subtitle: A one-line fix to the MIB authoring guidelines so copyright notices name the IETF Trust.

tldr.problem: RFC 4181 gives copyright notice templates that name the Internet Society, but the IETF Trust had been created.
tldr.mechanism: In the templates in Section 3.7 of RFC 4181, every occurrence of 'The Internet Society' is replaced with 'The IETF Trust'.
tldr.outcome: This brings RFC 4181 into line with the earlier notice changes in RFC 4748. The update has no impact on Internet security.

today: RFC 4841 is a Best Current Practice that updates RFC 4181. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why the Update
sections.content: The creation of the IETF Trust led to updates to the copyright notices required by RFC 3978, published in RFC 4748. This document is a Best Current Practice (BCP 111) that updates RFC 4181, 'Guidelines for Authors and Reviewers of MIB Documents', to match those changes.
sections.eli5: The rights moved to a new owner, so a guide that named the old owner needed fixing.

sections.title: The Change to Section 3.7
sections.content: The only change is to Section 3.7 of RFC 4181. In the copyright notice templates there, all occurrences of 'The Internet Society' are replaced with 'The IETF Trust'.
sections.eli5: Wherever the guide said the old name, it now says the new one.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The RFC states that the updates in this document have no impact on the security of the Internet.
sections.eli5: Changing a name on a notice does not make anything less safe.

references.text: Bradner, S., "IETF Rights in Contributions", BCP 78, RFC 3978, March 2005.
Bradner, S., "RFC 3978 Update to Recognize the IETF Trust", BCP 78, RFC 4748, October 2006.
